blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — valproate reproductive safety counseling
stem: A client of childbearing potential taking valproate asks why pregnancy planning and contraception are emphasized. Which response by the nurse is most accurate?

options.A: Valproate can cause major congenital malformations and neurodevelopmental harm, some of which may arise very early; effective contraception and regular risk counseling are recommended.
options.B: Valproate's main pregnancy concern is neonatal toxicity later in gestation, so contraception and preconception counseling provide little additional protection before pregnancy is recognized.
options.C: Folic acid supplementation is considered adequate protection against valproate-associated neural-tube and cognitive risks, so contraception counseling can be de-emphasized.
options.D: Valproate is associated with structural birth defects, but current labeling does not link in-utero exposure with decreased IQ or other neurodevelopmental disorders in children.

rationale: Current DailyMed labeling states that valproate can cause major congenital malformations, including neural-tube defects, and can cause decreased IQ and neurodevelopmental disorders after in-utero exposure. Because these fetal risks may occur very early in pregnancy, women of childbearing potential should use effective contraception when valproate treatment is necessary and should receive regular counseling about pregnancy risks and benefits. Therefore A is the best answer. B wrongly shifts the major fetal-risk discussion to later gestation. C overstates folic acid; the labeling states that it is not known whether folic acid reduces valproate-associated neural-tube-defect or decreased-IQ risk. D incorrectly denies the labeled neurodevelopmental risks.
educational_objective: Explain that valproate can cause major congenital malformations and neurodevelopmental harm, including risks that may occur very early in pregnancy, so effective contraception and regular pregnancy-risk counseling are important when treatment is necessary.
source_organization: DailyMed (U.S. National Library of Medicine); packager: Camber Pharmaceuticals, Inc.
source_document_title: Divalproex Sodium Extended-Release Tablets — Prescribing Information
source_locator: Warnings and Precautions §5.2 Structural Birth Defects; §5.3 Decreased IQ and Neurodevelopmental Disorders Following in utero Exposure; §5.4 Use in Women of Childbearing Potential: valproate can cause major congenital malformations and neurodevelopmental harm; fetal risks may occur very early in pregnancy; effective contraception and regular counseling are advised when treatment is necessary; folic acid supplementation is recommended, but it is not known whether it reduces valproate-associated neural-tube-defect or decreased-IQ risk.
source_claim_supported: Valproate exposure can cause major congenital malformations and neurodevelopmental harm; some fetal risks may occur very early in pregnancy, effective contraception and regular counseling are advised, and folic acid is not known to eliminate valproate-specific fetal risks.
blueprint_locator: Printed p. 38, Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: educate client about medications; review pertinent data prior to medication administration; evaluate client response to medication.
candidate_reasons_resolved: Rewrote A/B/C/D with parallel explanatory structure and more comparable lengths.
Removed the isolated absolute-word pattern and the uniquely longest correct-answer cue while preserving a single source-supported best answer.
audit_note: Clinical content was re-audited from zero after revision. A matches current labeling. B incorrectly delays the core fetal-risk issue, C overstates folic-acid protection, and D denies labeled neurodevelopmental harm. No second defensible answer remains and the original cueing pattern is resolved.
